verses.1: And the war became widespread between the house of Saul and the house of David. David went out and became stronger. Meanwhile, the house of Saul continued to weaken.
verses.2: And David had sons in Hebron. And in their inheritance was the town of Amnon, in the land of Judah.
verses.3: And they changed it into a beautiful ornament for the queen of Naboli, the daughter of Karmeli, and Abshalom, the daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur.
verses.4: And the fourth is Adoniyah, son of Hagith; and the fifth is Shephtiyah, son of Avital.
verses.5: And the Shishiy will be angry at the daughters of David. These were born to David in his own household.
verses.6: And during the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner became stronger in the house of Saul.
verses.7: And Shaul Pilgesh’s name was Ritzfah Bat-Ayah. He said to Avner, “Why have you come to Pilgesh, my father?”
verses.8: And Abner was very angry at the words of the man from Bosher. He said, “I, the dog’s head, who belongs to Judah today, will do a miracle for your father Shaul’s house, for his brothers and their enemies. Do not let David defeat me today. May disaster befall me today.”
verses.9: “Thus will God do to Abner. He will be honored, for just as Jehovah has blessed David, so too will I honor him.”
verses.10: To carry the Queen from Sheol, and to establish David’s throne over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beer Sheva.
verses.11: And he could no longer restore Abner’s honor in his eyes.
verses.12: And Abner sent messengers to David, under his command, with these words: “To which land did you swear your covenant? Now, my hand is with you, and I will help you to defeat all of Israel.”
verses.13: And he said, “Good. I will make a covenant with you. But there is one thing I ask of you: Do not look at my face. Only bring the chest of Shelah’s daughter when you come to see me.”
verses.14: And David sent messengers to Shechem, the daughter of Saul, with these words: “Give me back my wife, along with the chest that I inherited from her, along with its contents, which consisted of a hundred silver coins.”
verses.15: And he sent a man with a staff, and he took her away from among the people of Phaltiel son of Laiš.
verses.16: And she went away, walking away. She followed behind her lover all the way to the border. Then she said to him, “Abner, go back.”
verses.17: And Abner said to the elders of Israel, “Also, Tamul and Shilshom, you too should ask David to be king over you.”
verses.18: And now, do as Jehovah has commanded David: “In David’s hand my people Israel will be saved from the hands of Philistines and from all their enemies.”
verses.19: And Abner also spoke to Benyamin’s ears. Then Abner went and spoke to David’s ears about everything that was good in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of all the people of Benyamin.
verses.20: And Abner went to David’s house. With him were forty men. David did what was right for Abner and the men who were with him.
verses.21: And Abner said to David, “I will go and bring all of Israel to your king. He will make you his ruler and queen over all those who follow you.” Then David sent Abner away, and he went away in peace.
verses.22: And behold, the servants of David and Joab came from Gideon. They brought back a great amount of plunder with them. But Abner was not with David during this time; he went away in peace.
verses.23: And Joab and all the men who came with him reported to Joab, “Absalom is dead. He has been killed by the king.” Then Joab sent Absalom away, and he went away in peace.
verses.24: And Joab went to the king and said, “What have you done? Here comes Abner to see you. Why did you send him here?” Then he went away.
verses.25: You know that Abner, son of Naarah, will come to you. You will know what your fate is, and you will also know what awaits you. You will know everything that you do.
verses.26: Joab went out from David’s presence. He sent out the murderers after Abner. They took Abner away from his prison. David didn’t know about this at all.
verses.27: And Abner sat down with his men. Joab led him into the courtyard, so that he could talk with him. There, at that place, Abner died from blood loss. His brother Elah was also killed.
verses.28: And David heard this from behind him. He said, “Naked I am; and my kingdom will be with the LORD forever, from the time of Avner son of Nar.
verses.29: They will mourn over the head of Joab, and all the houses of his father’s family. No one from the house of Joab will be spared; both those who are healthy and those who are sick will be destroyed. They will be thrown into the grave, without any hope of survival.
verses.30: And Yoav and Abishai, his brothers, killed Abner because he had killed their fellow soldier, Asahel, in the battle.
verses.31: And David said to Joab and to all the people who had been captured by him, “Put on your armor and go before Abner.” Then King David went after the captains.
verses.32: And they buried Abner in his tomb. Then the king wept bitterly. All the people also wept over Abner’s grave.
verses.33: And the king built a palace for Abner. He said, “May Nabal die!”
verses.34: Your hands are not bound, and your feet are not shackled. You fell before the children of Avla. All the people gathered together to weep over you.
verses.35: And all the people came to offer bread as an offering to David. David said, “May God do this for me! I will eat this bread before sunrise.”
verses.36: And all the people recognized it, and they praised God for all that the king did in the eyes of all the people.
verses.37: And all the people and all of Israel knew on that day that it wasn’t the king who decided to kill Abner son of Ner.
verses.38: And the king said to his servants, “Do not know that the high priest and great man has fallen today in Israel.”
verses.39: And I, today, am happy and at ease, as a king. But these people are children of darkness; they are more difficult to deal with than I am. May Jehovah reward those who do evil with their own evil deeds.
